outputs.L1: Disclosed herein are a method and system for determining an overall value rating or value estimate for a product to be offered for sale or lease. The method includes identifying a product type associated with the product and determining a set of attributes corresponding to the identified product type. The method further includes calculating a value score unit size for the product based on statistical data relating to the product and the product type, determining an attribute value multiplier associated with each attribute in the set of attributes, and presenting an attribute template (130) to a seller associated with the product to be offered for sale or lease, the attribute template including the set of attributes. The method receives data from the seller relating to each attribute in the set of attributes (140). For each attribute in the attribute template, the method determines an attribute rating value based on the received data and the attribute value multiplier associated with that attribute (150), and then determines the overall rating value (160) based on a sum of the attribute rating values and an asking price submitted by the seller.
outputs.L2: Provided are a system and method for calculating a total value rating or estimated value for a product intended to be sold or leased. The process involves identifying the category of the product and establishing a group of attributes corresponding to that product category. A value-score unit size for the product is computed using statistical information associated with both the product and its category. The method also assigns an attribute value multiplier to each attribute in the identified group and supplies the seller of the product with an attribute template (130) containing those attributes. Information relating to every attribute in the group is then obtained from the seller (140). For each attribute listed in the template, an attribute rating value is calculated from the submitted information and the multiplier tied to that attribute (150). Finally, an overall rating value is produced (160) from the combined total of the attribute rating values together with the asking price provided by the seller.
outputs.L3:
The method and system are designed to determine an overall value rating or value estimate for a product that is being offered for sale or lease. This rating provides a comparative indication of whether the product represents a favorable value, taking into account both the characteristics of the product and the price requested by the seller.

To begin, the method identifies the type or category of the product being offered. Once the product type is determined, the system selects a relevant set of attributes associated with that product type. These attributes may vary depending on the nature of the product. For example, a vehicle may be evaluated based on mileage, model year, condition, trim level, and accident history, while a real estate property may be evaluated based on location, square footage, number of bedrooms, age, and condition.

The method then calculates a value score unit size using statistical data associated with the product and comparable products within the same product type. This statistical data may include historical transaction prices, current market listings, lease rates, demand indicators, depreciation data, or other market-based information. The value score unit size provides a basis for measuring the impact that individual product attributes have on the overall value of the product.

The system presents an attribute template to the seller. The attribute template includes fields corresponding to the relevant attributes identified for the particular product type. The seller enters or confirms information for each attribute, such as condition, age, features, specifications, usage history, or other relevant characteristics. The system receives and processes this seller-provided data in connection with the selected attribute template.

Using the seller-provided attribute data, the system determines rating values for the individual attributes. These attribute rating values are then combined with the seller’s asking price to determine an overall rating value for the product. The resulting overall rating may indicate, for example, whether the product is priced below market value, at market value, or above market value based on its attributes and comparable statistical data. In this way, the method and system provide a structured and data-driven assessment of the value of a product offered for sale or lease.
outputs.L4:
A method and system are provided for determining an overall value rating or value estimate for a product that is being offered for sale, lease, rental, or other transfer. The system first identifies the type or category of the product, such as a vehicle, real estate property, item of equipment, consumer good, or other asset. Once the product type has been identified, the system determines a set of attributes that are relevant to evaluating the value of that type of product. These attributes may include physical characteristics, performance features, age, condition, location, brand, model, usage history, included accessories, service records, warranties, or any other factors that may affect market value.

For each product type, the system may maintain or access statistical data relating to comparable products. This statistical data can include historical sale prices, lease prices, asking prices, market averages, depreciation trends, demand information, and other valuation data. From this information, the system calculates a value score unit size, which provides a basis for converting differences in product attributes into numerical rating values. The value score unit size may be derived from market averages, price ranges, standard deviations, or other statistical measures that reflect how particular attributes influence the value of comparable products.

The seller, lessor, or other offering party is then provided with an attribute template corresponding to the identified product type. The template prompts the seller to enter or select information describing the product being offered. For example, the template may request information about the product’s make, model, year, size, mileage, condition, configuration, included features, defects, upgrades, or other relevant characteristics. The completed template supplies the system with a structured description of the product, allowing the product to be evaluated consistently against similar products.

After receiving the completed attribute template, the system assigns rating values to the product’s attributes. Each attribute may be associated with an attribute value multiplier that reflects the relative importance of that attribute to the product’s market value. More significant attributes may receive larger multipliers, while less significant attributes may receive smaller multipliers. The system applies these multipliers to the attribute information provided by the seller and calculates weighted rating values for the product. Positive attributes may increase the product’s rating, while negative attributes may reduce it.

The system then combines the weighted attribute rating values with the seller’s asking price, lease price, or other proposed transaction amount. By comparing the product’s attributes and asking price against statistical data and comparable market offerings, the system produces an overall value rating or value estimate. This rating may indicate whether the product appears to be priced above market value, below market value, or in line with comparable products. The rating may be presented as a numerical score, a percentage, a grade, a ranking, a price estimate, or another form of value indicator.

The resulting overall value rating helps buyers, sellers, lessors, lessees, brokers, marketplaces, and other participants assess the relative value of the product. Buyers may use the rating to determine whether the asking price is reasonable, while sellers may use it to adjust pricing or improve the attractiveness of the listing. Online marketplaces may use the rating to sort, rank, highlight, or compare listings. In this way, the method and system provide a standardized, data-based approach for evaluating products offered for sale or lease by combining product-specific attributes, statistical market information, attribute weighting, and asking price data into a single overall value assessment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a method and system that calculates an overall value rating for a product offered for sale or lease using product attributes, statistical data, seller inputs, and asking price.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system are disclosed for determining an overall value rating for a product offered for sale or lease. Product attribute data associated with the product is received, including one or more characteristics of the product, and statistical data corresponding to comparable products is obtained from one or more data sources. Seller-provided inputs relating to condition, features, availability, terms, or other product-specific factors are further received, together with an asking price for sale or lease of the product. A valuation engine processes the product attribute data, statistical data, seller inputs, and asking price to generate one or more comparative metrics, including an estimated market value or expected price range. The asking price is compared with the comparative metrics and adjusted based on weighted product and seller factors to calculate an overall value rating. The overall value rating may be output for display to a prospective buyer or lessee, stored in a database, used to rank or filter product listings, or updated dynamically in response to changes in market data, seller inputs, or asking price.

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you draft a "Disclosed herein..." description of an invention for determining a value estimate of a product, including steps like identifying product type, selecting attributes, applying multipliers, receiving seller data, and calculating a final rating?
counterfactuals.output:
Disclosed herein are systems, methods, and non-transitory computer-readable media for determining a value estimate of a product. In some embodiments, a computerized valuation system receives product information associated with a product to be evaluated and identifies a product type corresponding to the product. Based at least in part on the identified product type, the system selects a set of product attributes relevant to valuation of the product. The product attributes may include, by way of non-limiting example, brand, model, age, condition, usage level, size, material, category, market demand, geographic location, prior sale data, listing history, warranty status, or any other attribute affecting product value.

In some embodiments, the system assigns or retrieves one or more attribute values corresponding to the selected product attributes. The attribute values may be received from a seller, extracted from images or text associated with the product, obtained from a database, inferred using machine learning, or determined using a combination thereof. The system may further receive seller-provided data, including one or more of an asking price, product condition description, photographs, purchase date, original purchase price, usage history, maintenance history, repair history, location, shipping availability, or seller rating.

In some embodiments, the valuation system applies one or more multipliers to the selected product attributes or corresponding attribute values. Each multiplier may represent a relative effect of a corresponding attribute on the estimated value of the product. For example, a condition multiplier may increase or decrease the value estimate based on whether the product is new, like new, used, refurbished, damaged, or nonfunctional. A demand multiplier may adjust the value estimate based on current market demand for the identified product type. A depreciation multiplier may adjust the value estimate based on product age or time since purchase. A seller-confidence multiplier may adjust the value estimate based on completeness or reliability of seller-provided data.

In some embodiments, a baseline value is determined for the product based on the identified product type. The baseline value may be obtained from historical transaction data, manufacturer suggested retail price data, marketplace listing data, auction data, catalog data, third-party pricing data, or a valuation model. The system may calculate an adjusted value by applying the one or more multipliers to the baseline value and/or to intermediate attribute scores. In certain embodiments, the system calculates a final rating for the product based on the adjusted value and one or more confidence measures. The final rating may include a numerical score, a price estimate, a value range, a condition grade, a seller recommendation, or a combination thereof.

In one embodiment, a method for determining a value estimate of a product comprises: receiving, by one or more processors, product data associated with a product; identifying, by the one or more processors, a product type of the product based at least in part on the product data; selecting, based on the identified product type, a plurality of valuation attributes relevant to the product type; receiving seller data corresponding to at least a subset of the plurality of valuation attributes; determining attribute scores for the plurality of valuation attributes using the seller data and one or more stored valuation rules; applying one or more multipliers to the attribute scores or to a baseline value associated with the product type; calculating an adjusted value estimate for the product based on the applied multipliers; and generating a final rating corresponding to the product based on the adjusted value estimate.

In some embodiments, the final rating is transmitted to a seller device, marketplace platform, valuation database, or listing generation system. The final rating may be used to recommend a listing price, automatically populate a product listing, determine whether the product satisfies a resale threshold, rank the product relative to comparable products, or present a confidence score indicating reliability of the value estimate.

In some embodiments, the system dynamically updates one or more multipliers based on subsequent market data, completed sales, seller feedback, buyer behavior, or changes in demand. The multipliers may be manually configured, automatically learned using a machine-learning model, or selected from a lookup table associated with the identified product type. In certain embodiments, different multiplier sets are applied to different product types, thereby enabling the system to account for product-specific valuation factors.

In some embodiments, the system further validates the seller data by comparing the seller data with independently obtained data. For example, an image analysis module may determine a condition score from one or more images of the product, and the condition score may be compared to a seller-provided condition description. If a discrepancy is detected, the system may reduce a confidence score, request additional information from the seller, or modify a corresponding multiplier. In this manner, the system provides a more accurate and reliable value estimate for the product.

Accordingly, the disclosed technology enables automated, consistent, and scalable determination of a product value estimate by identifying a product type, selecting valuation attributes associated with the product type, receiving seller-specific data, applying valuation multipliers, and calculating a final product rating or value estimate.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal patent summary for a system that presents an attribute template to a seller and computes attribute rating values to determine whether a product's sale or lease price is a good value.
counterfactuals.output:
A system is provided for evaluating whether a sale or lease price for a product represents a favorable value based on product attributes. The system includes one or more computing devices configured to present an attribute template to a seller, the attribute template including a plurality of attribute fields associated with characteristics of a product offered for sale or lease. The system receives seller-provided attribute information through the attribute template and stores the attribute information in association with the product.

The system further includes a valuation engine configured to process the attribute information and compute one or more attribute rating values corresponding to respective product attributes. The attribute rating values may be determined by applying predefined rating criteria, weighting factors, comparison data, market data, historical transaction data, or combinations thereof. The computed attribute rating values are used to generate an overall value indication for the product relative to the product’s sale or lease price.

In operation, the system compares the sale or lease price with an expected or reference value derived at least in part from the attribute rating values. Based on the comparison, the system determines whether the sale or lease price is a good value. The system may generate and transmit an output indicating the value determination to a seller, buyer, lessee, marketplace platform, or other user interface. The output may include an overall rating, attribute-specific ratings, a recommendation, a value score, or an indication that the product is priced favorably, unfavorably, or within an acceptable range.

The system thereby provides a structured, attribute-based mechanism for assessing product value, improving consistency in pricing evaluation and assisting users in making informed sale or lease decisions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert this invention idea into patent application language: a platform evaluates products for sale by using product type, attribute sets, statistical score units, attribute multipliers, seller-entered attribute data, and asking price to produce an overall value score.
counterfactuals.output:
A computer-implemented platform for evaluating products offered for sale is disclosed. The platform receives product information associated with a product listing, including a product type, one or more seller-provided attribute values, and an asking price. Based on the product type, the platform selects an applicable attribute set comprising a plurality of product attributes relevant to valuation of the product. Each attribute in the attribute set is associated with at least one statistical score unit and at least one attribute multiplier.

The platform processes the seller-provided attribute values by comparing the values to corresponding statistical score units for the selected product type. The platform applies the attribute multipliers to generate weighted attribute scores for the product. The weighted attribute scores are combined with pricing information, including the asking price, to generate an overall value score representing a relative value of the product listing. The overall value score may be displayed to a buyer, seller, marketplace operator, or other user to facilitate evaluation, comparison, ranking, pricing, or purchasing decisions.

In one embodiment, the platform comprises one or more processors and one or more non-transitory computer-readable storage media storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the platform to: receive a product type for a product offered for sale; identify an attribute set associated with the product type; receive seller-entered attribute data corresponding to at least a portion of the attribute set; retrieve statistical score units associated with the attribute set; apply attribute multipliers to the seller-entered attribute data and the statistical score units; receive an asking price for the product; and calculate an overall value score based on the applied attribute multipliers, the statistical score units, the seller-entered attribute data, and the asking price.

The overall value score may be used to normalize products of the same or similar product type, identify undervalued or overvalued listings, recommend listing prices, sort search results, generate buyer-facing value indicators, or provide seller feedback regarding the competitiveness of a listing.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
